Content: “Our translation proceeded in the following way: Abraham Ibn Daud [a Jewish scholar born in Muslim Spain] took the text and read aloud the Arabic words `text(one)` at a time, while Archdeacon Domingo Gundisalvo [a Christian scholar] wrote down the Latin equivalent to each of these words as he heard them.”
Copyright: Introductory note in the Latin translation of a treatise by eleventh-century Muslim philosopher Ibn Sina. The translation was produced in Christian-controlled Spain, circa `text(1150)`.
